relations.myth: The Igigi perform compulsory labor for seven Anunnaki
relations.note: Seven senior Anunnaki impose exhausting canal and earthwork labor on the Igigi.
Later cosmology distinguishes heavenly Igigi from chthonic or subterranean Anunnaki.

relations.myth: Divine assemblies acclaim the supreme god
relations.note: Both collectives serve and acclaim the supreme deity within the ordered cosmos.

relations.myth: Overlapping numerical classifications of the gods
relations.note: Learned texts sometimes apply both names to apparently overlapping populations of gods.

relations.myth: Council responding to the Igigi revolt
relations.note: Anu joins the senior gods deliberating after the Igigi surround Enlil's sanctuary.
The Igigi labor under Enlil's authority, digging waterways and carrying earth.
They burn their work gear and surround Enlil's sanctuary demanding relief.
Nusku asks who began hostilities; the Igigi collectively accept responsibility.

relations.myth: Creation of humanity after the labor revolt
relations.note: Ea proposes creating humans to assume the Igigi's intolerable labor burden.

relations.myth: Ea as sage of the Igigi
relations.note: A first-millennium prayer gives Ea the hierarchical title sage of the Igigi.

relations.myth: Creation of humanity after the labor revolt
relations.note: The birth goddess creates humans with Ea to relieve the Igigi's labor.

relations.myth: Slaying of the god used to create humanity
relations.note: His flesh and blood create humans who inherit the Igigi's former work.

relations.myth: Opening administration of the divine labor order
relations.note: Ninurta belongs to the senior administration governing the Igigi's labor.

relations.myth: Recovery of the Tablet of Destinies
relations.note: Ninurta defeats Anzû and restores the cosmic authority governing the Igigi.
The Igigi work within the hierarchy administered by the canal-controller Ennugi.
Anu and Enlil elevate Marduk within the Igigi's divine constituency.
The Igigi participate in Marduk's elevation and acclaim his supreme names.

relations.myth: Building and dedication of Babylon and Esagil
relations.note: The Igigi obey Marduk's settlement, build his sacred city, and attend its dedication.
The Igigi identify or assent to Qingu as the culpable rebel.

relations.myth: Theft of the Tablet of Destinies
relations.note: After stealing the tablet, Anzû claims authority to command every Igigi.
The heavenly Igigi witness or suffer the universal disorder caused by Erra.

relations.myth: Erra's disruption of the cosmic order
relations.note: Išum and the Igigi appear in the same cosmic drama without direct encounter.
Hymns call Ištar pre-eminent among or exalted above the Igigi.
Hymns place Sîn above the Igigi or call him their light.
Liturgical texts describe the Igigi as regulating or attending Sîn's rites.
The Igigi belong to the divine assembly before which Šamaš exercises judgment.
Neo-Assyrian theology places the Igigi beneath Aššur's universal authority.
Lahmu appears alongside the Igigi in the assembly supporting Marduk's elevation.
Lahamu appears alongside the Igigi in the assembly supporting Marduk's elevation.
